properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes: The agreement THE COAL AUTHORITY AND ENERGYBUILD MINING LIMITED Aberpergwm Colliery, https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/66c84ea0d36b5c32dbdf9805/Aberpergwm_Agreement_and_Notice_2024_Documents.pdf, August 21 2024,  between the Coal Authority and mine operators, EnergyBuild Mining Ltd describes the mining license and seam mining areas.  Page 1 of the plans in https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/66c73a65f86d967e6161820e/Aberpergwm_Agreement_and_Notice_Plans_2024.pdf shows the boundary encompassing all of the licensed seam mining areas. The license boundary is also found in the License Area layer of the Coal Mining section of the Mining Remediation Authority Map Viewer at https://web.archive.org/web/20250416191408/https://experience.arcgis.com/experience/39bb823f1bf44b51b992019a3aaeac60/page/Coal-Mining#data_s=id%3AdataSource_19-195d867b53a-layer-32%3A1340. Three overlapping licensed areas are shown, only one with a site name of Aberpergwm (Licence Reference: DM/95/0025/C, Licence Type: Underground, Status: Current, Site Name: Aberpergwm GLOBALID  A7AFD5EF-B0F4-421D-B5C2-24B3F326105B.   Given the August 21 2024 date of the license agreement, it's assumed that this boundary includes all recent expansion plans. The area of this boundary is approx 2,700 hectares, or 27 sq km.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes: The agreement THE COAL AUTHORITY AND ENERGYBUILD MINING LIMITED Aberpergwm Colliery, https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/66c84ea0d36b5c32dbdf9805/Aberpergwm_Agreement_and_Notice_2024_Documents.pdf, August 21 2024,  between the Coal Authority and mine operators, EnergyBuild Mining Ltd describes the mining license and seam mining areas.  Page 1 of the plans in https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/66c73a65f86d967e6161820e/Aberpergwm_Agreement_and_Notice_Plans_2024.pdf shows the boundary encompassing all of the licensed seam mining areas. The license boundary is also found in the License Area layer of the Coal Mining section of the Mining Remediation Authority Map Viewer at https://web.archive.org/web/20250416191408/https://experience.arcgis.com/experience/39bb823f1bf44b51b992019a3aaeac60/page/Coal-Mining#data_s=id%3AdataSource_19-195d867b53a-layer-32%3A1340. Three overlapping licensed areas are shown, only one with a site name of Aberpergwm (Licence Reference: DM/95/0025/C, Licence Type: Underground, Status: Current, Site Name: Aberpergwm GLOBALID  A7AFD5EF-B0F4-421D-B5C2-24B3F326105B.   Given the August 21 2024 date of the license agreement, it's assumed that this boundary includes all recent expansion plans. The area of this boundary is approx 2,700 hectares, or 27 sq km.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
Based on section 2.1 figure 2.1 on page 3, and table 3.1 on page 5, of the Ashton Coal/Yancoal Annual Review for Ashton Coal Project for 2023, published in March 2024, https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.yancoal.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Ashton-Annual-Review_March-2024.pdf, Ashton Coal Project is comprised of the following components: (1) a decomissioned north-east open cut (NEOC) used for coarse reject storage and coal fines, north of the A15 New England Highway, in mining leases ML1529 and ML1533; (2) the Ashton undeground mine, south of the A15 New England Highway, in mining lease ML1533; (3) a coal handling and preparation plant and rail loadout, north of the A15 New England Highway in mining ML1533; (4) integration with part of the Ravensworth underground mine, owned by Glencore, in mining leases ML1834, ML1835, ML1836 and ML1837; (5) the south east open cut in mining lease ML1696 (mining here prevented by Wendy Bowman not selling her land to Yancoal).

This boundary component is comprised of the Ashton underground coal mine and the northeast open cut covered by mining leases ML1529, ML1533 and ML1623. 

Mining lease polygons were extracted from the Geological Survey NSW GeoServer web feature service 
https://web.archive.org/web/20250427032655/https://www.resources.nsw.gov.au/geological-survey/products-and-data/gis-web-services.

The area of this boundary is 9 sq km.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
Based on section 2.1 figure 2.1 on page 3, and table 3.1 on page 5, of the Ashton Coal/Yancoal Annual Review for Ashton Coal Project for 2023, published in March 2024, https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.yancoal.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Ashton-Annual-Review_March-2024.pdf, Ashton Coal Project is comprised of the following components: (1) a decomissioned north-east open cut (NEOC) used for coarse reject storage and coal fines, north of the A15 New England Highway, in mining leases ML1529 and ML1533; (2) the Ashton undeground mine, south of the A15 New England Highway, in mining lease ML1533; (3) a coal handling and preparation plant and rail loadout, north of the A15 New England Highway in mining ML1533; (4) integration with part of the Ravensworth underground mine, owned by Glencore, in mining leases ML1834, ML1835, ML1836 and ML1837; (5) the south east open cut in mining lease ML1696 (mining here prevented by Wendy Bowman not selling her land to Yancoal).

This boundary component is comprised of the Ashton underground coal mine and the northeast open cut covered by mining leases ML1529, ML1533 and ML1623. 

Mining lease polygons were extracted from the Geological Survey NSW GeoServer web feature service 
https://web.archive.org/web/20250427032655/https://www.resources.nsw.gov.au/geological-survey/products-and-data/gis-web-services.

The area of this boundary is 9 sq km.

The underground, punch longwall mine, Broadmeadow, has been developed in an existing highwall of the open cut operation.". The underground mining boundary overlaps with the surface mining operations of the Goonyella-Riverside Coal Mine, which is also owned by BHP Coal Pty Ltd and operates under the same Environmental Authority (EPML00853413) permit as the underground Broadmeadow Coal Mine. The underground mining boundary is the perimeter of the Broadmeadow Underground Mine area shown in Figure 1-2 PROJECT SITE of ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT STATEMENT Redhill Mining Lease, https://web.archive.org/web/20221208033144/https://www.bhp.com/-/media/bhp/regulatory-information-media/coal/bhp-billiton-mitsubishi-alliance/red-hill/red-hill-mining-lease-project-draft-environmental-impact-statement-eis/131213_coal_bma_redhill_section01introduction.pdf (publish date not given). properties.Boundaries and methane sources 2: notes:
The Aquila mine is a part of the Capcoal complex which comprises Capcoal open cut mine, Grasstree mine, Aquila mine, the Coal Handling and Preparation Plant and ancillary infrastructure. The Aquila long wall mine replaces Grasstree mine as of 2022, as described in  https://web.archive.org/web/20240710230944/https://www.nsenergybusiness.com/projects/aquila-metallurgical-coal-mine-australia.

The Aquila long wall mine resides within the southern section of the mining lease ML 1831 (German Creek). The mine area overlaps the retired Aquila bord and pillar mine and the old Grasstree mine.

The mine boundary is the Aquila Longwall Mining Area shown in figure 2 on the 221st page of 2020 EPBC 2018/8171 Independent Compliance Audit - Grasstree Mine EPBC Audit 2018:8171, https://web.archive.org/web/20250327203347/https://australia.angloamerican.com/~/media/Files/A/Anglo-American-Group-v5/Australia/sustainability/environment/EPBC2018_8171_2020_Ind_Audit.pdf

The area of the extracted mine boundary is 25 square kilometers.

Section 2.1 Project Overview, page 6, of Public Environment Report Gregory Crinum Mine M-Block Extension, June 29 2023,
https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.sojitzblue.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Gregory-Crinum-Mine-M-Block-Extension-Project-EPBC-2021-9127-Public-Environment-Report-Jul-2023-Rev.-No.-7.pdf, describes the mining leases comprising the mine as MLs 1789, 1923, 70061, 7007. Undergound mining is located in ML 1923 in the southern eastern section of the boundary of the mining leases as shown in Figure 2.1: GCM mining infrastructure on page 7, and partially shown extended westwards from the southeastern corner in Figure 2: M-Block proposed open-cut and underground operations areas on page 6 of Offset Area Management Plan Gregory Crinum M-Block Extension 14 April 2023, https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.sojitzblue.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/GCM-M-Block-Expansion-Offset-Area-Management-Plan_V2.pdf. The area of the extracted boundary is 127 sq km.

Section 2.1 Project Overview, page 6, of Public Environment Report Gregory Crinum Mine M-Block Extension, June 29 2023,
https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.sojitzblue.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Gregory-Crinum-Mine-M-Block-Extension-Project-EPBC-2021-9127-Public-Environment-Report-Jul-2023-Rev.-No.-7.pdf, describes the mining leases comprising the mine as MLs 1789, 1923, 70061, 7007. Undergound mining is located in ML 1923 in the southern eastern section of the boundary of the mining leases as shown in Figure 2.1: GCM mining infrastructure on page 7, and partially shown extended westwards from the southeastern corner in Figure 2: M-Block proposed open-cut and underground operations areas on page 6 of Offset Area Management Plan Gregory Crinum M-Block Extension 14 April 2023, https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.sojitzblue.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/GCM-M-Block-Expansion-Offset-Area-Management-Plan_V2.pdf. The area of the extracted boundary is 127 sq km.

Mining lease geometries were extracted from the Queensland Mining Leases dataset (https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.data.qld.gov.au/dataset/queensland-mining-and-exploration-tenure-series/resource/f87794b8-7b9a-4732-89bb-56ccb2228d27).

The mining lease ML 70378 was corroborated against Figure 1 Moranbah Township and Grosvenor Mine Plan on page 7 of GROSVENOR COAL MINE Underground Operations PLN – Grosvenor Mine Overview issues 11/11/2015, https://web.archive.org/web/20250327195920/https://www.coalminesinquiry.qld.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0006/1620996/AGM.002.001.0818-Grosvenor-Mine-Overview-Plan.pdf. The 70378 permit was granted June 2012 and expires June 2047. The adjacent exploratory permit EPC 1454 (permit holder name : ANGLO COAL (GROSVENOR) PTY LTD) is also included in the boundary. The area of the 2 mining leases is approximately 118 square kilometers.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
Row 1 of Table 1 on page 6 of the Compliance report Byerwen Coal Project EPBC 2010/5778 6 March 2024 Byerwen Coal Project, Queensland EPBC 2010/5778 9 December 2022 to 8 December 2023, published 6 March 2024, https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.qcoal.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/240311-EPBC2010-5778-Annual-Compliance-Report.pdf, describes the project area in terms of mining lease applications 10355, 10356, 10357, 70434, 70435, 70436 and 700058. 

Figure 2.2 Sequential progress plot map, page 5, of the Byerwen Coal project: Coordinator-General’s evaluation report on the environmental impact statement, July 2014,  https://web.archive.org/web/20250417170244/https://eisdocs.dsdip.qld.gov.au/Completed%20Projects/Byerwen%20Coal/CGER/Coordinator-General%20s%20Evaluation%20Report%20for%20the%20Byerwen%20Coal%20project%20_signed_reduced%20size.pdf, shows the development over time of the 8 pits planned located in these leases.

Mining lease geometries were extracted from the Queensland Mining Leases dataset, https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.data.qld.gov.au/dataset/queensland-mining-and-exploration-tenure-series/resource/f87794b8-7b9a-4732-89bb-56ccb2228d27.

The boundary is the perimeter of these mining leases. The area of the boundary is 210 sq km.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes: Section 1.1 Project Overview and History of Progressive Rehabilitation and Closure Plan, March 2024, https://web.archive.org/web/20250327202352/https://storagesolutiondocsprod.blob.core.windows.net/register-documents-applications-prcp/PRCP-EPML00942413-V1_1_Applicationdocuments_Attachment_02.pdf describes the mining leases for the mine: ML 1832, ML 2004, ML 70241, ML 70327 and ML 70424 and Figure 2.5 of shows the mining lease areas. Mining lease details from the Queensland Mining Leases dataset https://web.archive.org/web/20250327173139/https://www.data.qld.gov.au/dataset/queensland-mining-and-exploration-tenure-series/resource/f87794b8-7b9a-4732-89bb-56ccb2228d27 : ML 1832 (Oaky Creek), granted June 1979, expiring June 2041; ML 70327 (Oaky East), granted March 2009, expiring June 2041;  ML 70424 (Oaky South East), granted July 2012, expiring July 2027;  ML 70241 (Sandy Creek), granted July 2001, expiring June 2041;  ML 2004 (Oaky Creek Extended), granted August 1993, expiring August 2035. The boundary is the perimeter of these mining leases and has an area of 176 sq km.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
The boundary is the outer perimeter of mining leases ML 1884, ML 70343 and ML 1904 shown in Figure 1: Clermont Mine Location and Tenements on page 5 of Clermont Open Cut Glencore Plan for INITIAL DEVELOPMENT PLAN: 1 JANUARY 2016 - 31 DECEMBER 2020 Clermont Mining Lease Application Wolfang #4 (ML1904), from Sep 14, 2016, https://web.archive.org/web/20240617114506/https://minedocs.com/21/Clermont-Initial-Development-Plan-2016-2020.pdf. Mining lease ML 70334, a conveyor belt leading to mining lease ML 1881, coal and water storage and part of the Blair Athol mine, are not included in the boundary. The source date of this pdf was determined by inspecting the pdf creation date.

Figure 2: Project Layout on page 9 of The Clearmont Coal Mine - Initial advice statement from 2003 https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.statedevelopment.qld.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0019/17344/ccm-ias.pdf, shows earlier versions of mining leases ML 1884 and ML 1904, the outer perimeter of which match closely the outer perimeter of the more recent  ML 1884, ML 70343 and ML 1904 mining leases.

Mining lease geometries were extracted from the Queensland Mining Leases dataset (https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.data.qld.gov.au/dataset/queensland-mining-and-exploration-tenure-series/resource/f87794b8-7b9a-4732-89bb-56ccb2228d27).

The area of the boundary is 32 sq km.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes: Coppabella mine is part of the Coppabella Moorvale Joint Venture (CMJV). From the Technical Report Summary Coppabella-Moorvale Joint Venture (CMJV) from 2/2022, https://web.archive.org/web/20230523200452/https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1064728/000106472822000008/btu_20211231xex964.htm, the table in section 1.2 Property Description lists mining leases for Coppabella mine as follows: ML 70161 (Johnson); ML 70163 (Johnson Extended); ML 70164 (Johnson Extended No. 2); ML 70236 (Coppabella East); ML 70237 (Coppabella South); ML 70384 (Johnson Extended No. 3); ML 70385 (Johnson Extended No. 4); ML 70386 (Johnson Extended No. 5); ML 70387 (Johnson Extended No. 6). Note that mining leases ML 70236 (Coppabella East) and ML 70237 (Coppabella South) both expired 2023. The boundary includes all nine mining leases above and has an area of approximately 39 sq km. Mining lease geometries were extracted from the Queensland Mining Leases dataset (https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.data.qld.gov.au/dataset/queensland-mining-and-exploration-tenure-series/resource/f87794b8-7b9a-4732-89bb-56ccb2228d27).

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
Coronado Global Resources Inc. (“Coronado”) Statement of Coal Resources and Reserves for the Curragh Mine Complex in Accordance with the JORC Code and United States SEC Regulation S-K 1300 as of December 31st 2023 Bowen Basin Queensland, Australia, published February 15, 2024, https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://minedocs.com/26/Curragh-TRS-S-K1300-12312023.pdf, providing a statement of Coal Resources and Coal Reserves estimates, shows in Tables 3.1 and 3.2 (pg 16) the mining leases and mining development leases for the mine.

The (non-development) mining leases includes the Curragh, Curragh extensions, Curragh A, Curragh North, Curragh Central, Curragh Central Extended, Curragh East, Curragh South and Curragh West No. 1 areas. Two surface pit mines are visible in Google Earth Pro satellite imagery from August 2023 in Curragh North, Curragh, Curragh A and Curragh East. The two pits cover approximately 34% of the area within the mining leases perimeter. The boundary is the perimeter of the mining leases and has an area of 197 sq km.

Mining lease geometries were extracted from the Queensland Mining Leases dataset (https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.data.qld.gov.au/dataset/queensland-mining-and-exploration-tenure-series/resource/f87794b8-7b9a-4732-89bb-56ccb2228d27).  Also according to this dataset,  mining leases ML 1878 and ML 80012 expired on May 31, 2024; ML 80112 is due to expire September 30 2025 and ML 80086 is due to expire October 31, 2025.

Also according to page 10 of the Statement of Coal Resources and Reserves for the Curragh Mine Complex, 'The Curragh mine includes a development underground project at Curragh North currently in operational readiness phase and planned to commence production in 2025.'.  The Coronado Australian Operations website https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://coronadoglobal.com/operations/australia also refers to information about the underground expansion, called Mammoth Underground and a waste mine coal gas pilot project.

Table 17: Daunia tenure, on page 61 of ASX ANNOUNCEMENT "Whitehaven Coal to acquire 100% of BMA’s Daunia and Blackwater coal mines through a compelling and transformational acquisition", published 18 October 2023, https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://whitehavencoal.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/WHC_Acquisition_of_Daunia_and_Blackwater_mines_announcement.pdf, shows the mining leases for Daunia mine : ML 1781 (Daunia), ML 70115 (Daunia East), ML
 70116 (Red Mountain). Figure 3: Primary tenures and layout of the Daunia Mine, on page 10 illustrates these mining lease boundaries and the mining areas and future potential mining contained within. Note that ML 70116 contains the coal handling and process plant but no apparent mining pits.

The boundary includes the three mining leases. The area of the boundary is 34 sq km.

Mining lease geometries were extracted from the Queensland Mining Leases dataset (https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.data.qld.gov.au/dataset/queensland-mining-and-exploration-tenure-series/resource/f87794b8-7b9a-4732-89bb-56ccb2228d27).

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
From the introduction on page 4 of Dawson Mine Supporting Information for Environmental Authority Amendment Environmental Authority EPML00565813 from 9/2024, https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://australia.angloamerican.com/~/media/Files/A/Anglo-American-Group-v5/Australia/landholder-information/Dawson%20Central%20and%20North/Part%202%20%20Application%20supporting%20document.pdf, Dawson Central and North Mine (DCN) consists of the following mining leases: ML 5591, ML 5592, ML 5593, ML 5596, ML 5597, ML 5598, ML 5599, ML 5600, ML 5601, ML 5603, ML 5604, ML 5606, ML 5607, ML 5611, ML 5630, ML 5643, ML 5644, ML 5646, ML 5650, ML 5656, ML 80032, ML 80034, ML 80070, ML 80142 and ML 80146, and the following exploration leases: EPC578, EPC894, EPC895, EPC988, EPC989, EPC1068, EPC1086.

From Section 3.1 Dawson South Mine, paragraph 3 of Supporting information for the Dawson South Mine Environmental Assessment Report from 3/2024, pages 1-2, https://web.archive.org/web/20250714134814/https://australia.angloamerican.com/~/media/Files/A/Anglo-American-Group-v5/Australia/landholder-information/dawson-south/a-ea-amd-100627125-support-info.pdf, the mining operations of Dawson South mine are located within mining leases ML 5657, ML 80160 and ML 80161.

The boundary is comprised of the above Dawson Central and North mine mining leases, and the Dawson South mine mining leases, but excludes the Moura seam gas pipeline lease ML 800032, and excludes the Dawson Central and North mine exploration leases.

Petroleum leases PL 94, PL 1048 and PL 1049, and pipline leases PPL 182, PPL 61 and PPL 26 are colocated and overlapping along the western edge of the mine boundary and coal seam gas facilities are visible in the eastern area of the mine boundary that contains mining leases ML 5644 and ML 5599. Undeground coal mining stopped in 1994 at the Dawson mining complex.

The area of the mine boundary is 308 sq km.

Mining lease geometries were extracted from the Queensland Mining Leases dataset (https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.data.qld.gov.au/dataset/queensland-mining-and-exploration-tenure-series/resource/f87794b8-7b9a-4732-89bb-56ccb2228d27).

"This mine operates under two adjacent subsoil land-use licenses КЗЛ 14886 ТЭ and КЗЛ 15045 ТЭ, as identified through the Official Portal of the Ministry of Economy of the Republic of Tuva: Construction of a Coal Mining Complex at the Mezhegeyskoye Deposit of the Ulug-Khem Coal Basin
(Официальный портал Министерства экономики Республики Тыва: Строительство угледобывающего комплекса на Межегейском месторождении Улуг-Хемского угольного бассейна), https://web.archive.org/web/20251224152222/https://mert-tuva.ru/old/directions/investment-policy/investment-projects/mejegey/index.htm, 2020. The boundary is the outer perimeter of these two licenses. The license КЗЛ 14886 ТЭ was issued on March 18, 2010, and is valid until March 22, 2030. The license КЗЛ 15045 ТЭ was issued on November 19, 2010, and is valid until November 8, 2030. The boundary for license КЗЛ 14886 ТЭ was extracted from the NedraExpert portal at https://web.archive.org/web/20251224154527/https://www.nedraexpert.ru/license/150551?ysclid=mjk45v4a5m702187839. The boundary for license КЗЛ 15045 ТЭ was extracted from the NedraExpert portal at https://web.archive.org/web/20251224154513/https://www.nedraexpert.ru/license/150925?ysclid=mjk4cw38y7618189831.The approximate area of the resulting boundary is 146 square km.

According to paragraph 3 of the introduction on page 4 of the Annual Compliance Report Drake Coal Mine EPBC 2010/5457 8 November 2023 to 7 November 2024, published 24 January 2025, Drake Coal Mine is wholly contained within Mining Leases 10349, 10350 and 10351, which cover an area of 9,215 Ha (92.15 sq km). These four mines are collectively operated and managed as an integrated mining operation by QCoal, and referred to as the QCoal Northern Hub (QNH).

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes: This mine operates under two subsoil land-use licenses КЕМ15030ТЭ and КЕМ11578ТЭ,as identified through the official Kuzbassgiproschaft (Кузбассгипрошахт) website,https://web.archive.org/web/20251208180730/https://kgsh.ru/mediacenter/1144/.The boundary is the outer perimeter of these two licenses,with internal gaps removed. The license КЕМ15030ТЭ was issued on November 1, 2010, and is valid until July 1, 2053. The western portion of the Raspadskaya-Koksovaya boundary overlaps with the eastern edge of the V.I. Lenin Underground Coal Mine boundary. The license КЕМ11578ТЭ was issued on June 17, 2003, and is valid until July 1, 2057. The boundary for license КЕМ15030ТЭ was extracted from the NedraExpert portal at https://web.archive.org/web/20251208163515/https://www.nedraexpert.ru/subsurface/1144754536/1. The boundary for license КЕМ11578ТЭ was extracted from the NedraExpert portal at https://web.archive.org/web/20251208153507/https://www.nedraexpert.ru/subsurface/1144750445/1. The approximate area of the resulting boundary is 20 square km.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes: The boundary was extracted from the Fording permit area shown in Figure 10-1: Drill Collar Location Plan on pg. 10-4 of the NI 43-101 Technical Report on Fording River Coal Operation, https://web.archive.org/web/20240716144338/https://minedocs.com/24/FordingRiver_TR_12312022.pdf, December 31, 2022. It includes a simplified outer boundary and excludes smaller inner boundaries in central and northern portion of the permit area. A portion of the southern permit boundary overlaps with the Greenhills coal mine permit boundary, owned by the same company. The NI 43-101 Technical Report on Greenhills Coal Operation report, https://web.archive.org/web/20240812193327/https://minedocs.com/24/Greenhills_TR_12312022.pdf, December 31, 2022, on page 4-2, states "Fording River Operations currently maintain the overlapping mineral tenure holdings as there is no mechanism within the Coal Act to subdivide the shared mineral tenure holdings,". Therefore, this overlapping area is included in the boundary. The approximate boundary area is 68.3 sq km.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes: The boundary was extracted from the Fording permit area shown in Figure 10-1: Drill Collar Location Plan on pg. 10-4 of the NI 43-101 Technical Report on Fording River Coal Operation, https://web.archive.org/web/20240716144338/https://minedocs.com/24/FordingRiver_TR_12312022.pdf, December 31, 2022. It includes a simplified outer boundary and excludes smaller inner boundaries in central and northern portion of the permit area. A portion of the southern permit boundary overlaps with the Greenhills coal mine permit boundary, owned by the same company. The NI 43-101 Technical Report on Greenhills Coal Operation report, https://web.archive.org/web/20240812193327/https://minedocs.com/24/Greenhills_TR_12312022.pdf, December 31, 2022, on page 4-2, states "Fording River Operations currently maintain the overlapping mineral tenure holdings as there is no mechanism within the Coal Act to subdivide the shared mineral tenure holdings,". Therefore, this overlapping area is included in the boundary. The approximate boundary area is 68.3 sq km.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
This mine operates under two adjacent subsoil land-use licenses, КЕМ13101ТЭ and КЕМ01871ТЭ, as identified through the State Register of Objects Having a Negative Impact on the Environment, maintained by Rosprirodnadzor (Государственный реестр объектов, оказывающих негативное воздействие на окружающую среду, Росприроднадзор), uonvos.rpn.gov.ru/rpn/pto-uonvos/onv_registry/card/78792/review?ysclid=mj8z933qik592243021, accessed December 2025.
The license КЕМ13101ТЭ was issued on April 5, 2005, and is valid until April 1, 2025. The license КЕМ01871ТЭ was issued on February 16, 2015, and is valid until February 16, 2035. The boundary for license КЕМ13101ТЭ was extracted from the NedraExpert portal at https://web.archive.org/web/20251216195340/https://www.nedraexpert.ru/license/147940?ysclid=mj8yqlx7nz438736704. The boundary for license КЕМ01871ТЭ was extracted from the NedraExpert portal at https://web.archive.org/web/20251216195537/https://www.nedraexpert.ru/subsurface/1200028012/1?ysclid=mj8z6eiju6394737718. The resulting mine boundary represents the outer perimeter of these two adjacent license areas. The approximate area of the resulting boundary is 8 square km.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: Full m: Gondudih Khas Kusunda Coal Mine, India, M2807
properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
Chapter 1 Introduction section 1.1 on the 29th page of the six monthly compliance report on Environmental Clearance Conditions for the period from April 2018 to Sept 2018 in respect of Cluster-VI Group of mines, https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.bcclweb.in/Environment%20Clearance/2018/HYC/HYC_Cluster%206.pdf, dated December 31 2018, describes the mine as part of Bharat Coking Coal Limited's Cluster VI which contains 4 mines: East Basseriya Colliery (OC), Basseriya colliery (UG), Gondudih Khas Kusunda colliery (OC) and Godhur Colliery (Mixed). According to BCCLs Kusundra Area webpage, https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://bcclweb.in/?page_id=6322, the leasehold area of the Gondudih Khas Kusunda Colliery is 410 hectares.

Plate 2: Surface Plan of Cluster VI on 23rd page of COMPLIANCE OF EC CONDITIONS of CLUSTER-VI EC order no.: J-11015/183/2011-1A.II (M), dated 26-08-2013 (October 2022 to March 2023), signed off on May 29, 2023 (15th page), https://web.archive.org/web/20240122193955/https://www.bcclweb.in/EC%20Compliance%201st%20October%2022%20to%2031st%20March%2023/cluster-VI.pdf, shows the boundaries of each of the mines in the cluster. The Gondudih Khas Kusunda colliery boundary was extracted from the colliery boundary for the mine shown in plate 2 and has an area of 386 hectares.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes: The Goonyella-Riverside Coal Mine is part of a BHP Coal Pty Ltd mining complex which also includes the underground Broadmeadow Mine. The boundary is specific to the open-cut surface mine, Goonyella-Riverside. The ventilation and degasification infrastructure found within the mine boundary are assumed to belong to the underground mining operations at the Broadmeadow Mine (M0016). The mine's individual mining lease boundaries were downloaded from the Queensland Spatial Catalogue, https://web.archive.org/web/20250703175324/https://www.data.qld.gov.au/dataset/queensland-mining-and-exploration-tenure-series/resource/5041f29f-7001-467c-803f-963c59da76c1, last updated in 2024. The relevant lease boundary numbers were confirmed in a 2017 Environmental Authority Permit document, https://web.archive.org/save/https://storagesolutiondocsprod.blob.core.windows.net/register-documents-ea/EPML00853413_20240226.pdf, and the associated boundary polygons were identified from the Queensland Spatial Catalogue data. The lease boundaries were merged into a single total boundary polygon in QGIS. The resultant polygon was simplified in Google Earth Pro to remove narrow roadway spaces within the greater boundary. The area of the polygon is approximately 174 square km. The boundary polygon overlaps with the mining boundary of the underground Broadmeadow Mine, which is also owned by BHP Coal Pty Ltd and operated under the same Environmental Authority (EPML00853413) permit as the Goonyella-Riverside Coal Mine.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes: The boundary was extracted from the Greenhills permit area shown in Figure 10-1: Drill Collar Location Plan on pg. 10-4 of the NI 43-101 Technical Report on Greenhills Coal Operation, https://web.archive.org/web/20240812193327/https://minedocs.com/24/Greenhills_TR_12312022.pdf, December 31, 2022. The boundary has been simplified by excluding small permitted areas peripheral to the main polygon and small inner boundaries within the main polygon. A portion of the northern permit boundary overlaps with the Fording River Operations coal mine permit boundary, owned by the same company. Page 4-2 states "Fording River Operations currently maintain the overlapping mineral tenure holdings as there is no mechanism within the Coal Act to subdivide the shared mineral tenure holdings"; therefore, this overlapping area is excluded from the Greenhills permit boundary here. The approximate boundary area is 36 sq km.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
The boundary is the underground mining area polygon extracted from the West Virginia Geological and Economic Survey (WVGES) resource at https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://atlas.wvgs.wvnet.edu/arcgis/rest/services/Coal_Web_Mercator/All_Mining_WM/MapServer. This resource was filtered for mine_name like %BECKLEY POCAHONTAS%, and the resulting polygon for mine_name 'BAY HILL NO 1 / BECKLEY POCAHONTAS MINE' was deholed and simplified using distance-based simplification with a tolerance of 25m. The mine mines the Pocahontas_3 coal seam. The area of this boundary is 26 sq km.

Important note: the following mine boundaries overlap the mine boundary and care should be taken when attempting methane source attribution: Eccles no 5 (Sewell coal seam), Eccles no 6 (Beckley coal seam), Sprague (Sewell coal seam), Crab orchard (Sewell coal seam), Crab orchard no 1 (Sewell coal seam), Crab orchard no 2 (Sewell coal seam) and 3 unknown mines.

properties.Measurements Methodology: The emissions data come from quarterly reports to the US Greenhouse Gas Reporting Data Program subpart FF, 'Total Quarterly Net Methane Emissions to the Atmosphere - Calculated Facility Total Quarterly Net CH4'. properties.Emissions Calculation Detail: The latest year for which both emissions data and GCMT production data were available was 2023. The emissions data for this year was 0.05342578 Mt CH4, taken from 'EPA GHG Envirofacts - SUBPART FF - UNDERGROUND COAL MINES table'. The production data for this year was 5.66 Mt coal, taken from data in 'Historic Production (2018-2025)'. Using this data, the emissions factor is 0.009439183745583038 million tonnes of methane per million tonnes of coal.
properties.Measurements Methodology: The emissions data come from quarterly reports to the US Greenhouse Gas Reporting Data Program subpart FF, 'Total Quarterly Net Methane Emissions to the Atmosphere - Calculated Facility Total Quarterly Net CH4'. These data are based on measurements at drainage stations and ventilation shafts and have been annualized by GEM.

(Предварительная экологическая оценка намечаемой корректировки проекта строительства угольной шахты «Инаглинская»), https://www.archive.org/details/inaglinskaya-coal-mine, page 5, 2021. The license ЯКУ 04565 ТЭ was issued on November 30, 2015, and is valid until December 25, 2026. The license ЯКУ 04564 ТЭ was issued on November 30, 2015, and is valid until June 1, 2025.The license ЯКУ 04639 ТЭ was issued on April 22, 2016, and is valid until April 30, 2041. The license ЯКУ 05093 ТЭ was issued on September 28, 2016, and is valid until February 24, 2032. License issuance and expiration dates were identified through the Rosnedra license registry, “Register of Subsoil Use Licenses as of January 1, 2024” («Реестр лицензий по состоянию на 01.01.2024 г.»), https://www.archive.org/details/register-of-subsoil-use-licenses-as-of-january-1-2024.The boundary for license ЯКУ 04565 ТЭ was extracted from the NedraExpert portal at https://web.archive.org/web/20251223182237/https://www.nedraexpert.ru/license/135788?ysclid=mjiwunfser782625186. The boundary for license ЯКУ 05093 ТЭ was extracted from the NedraExpert portal at <url>.  Polygon boundaries for subsoil licenses ЯКУ 04564 ТЭ and ЯКУ 04639 ТЭ were georeferenced using the Preliminary Environmental Assessment of the Proposed Adjustment to the Inaglinskaya Coal Mine Construction Project («Предварительная экологическая оценка намечаемой корректировки проекта строительства угольной шахты «Инаглинская»), page 94, https://www.archive.org/details/inaglinskaya-coal-mine, 2021. The resulting mine boundary represents the outer perimeter of these four adjacent license areas. The approximate area of the resulting boundary is 170 square km.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 2: notes: The Inaglinsky-1 plant, referred to in EIA documentation as a "mining and processing plant" (see under "Данные планируемой (намечаемой) хозяйственной и иной деятельности," available here: https://web.archive.org/web/20251009181707/https://o-v-o-s.ru/14/20305 "Корректировка проекта строительства шахты «Инаглинская» АО «ГОК «Инаглинский»," ОВОС: общественные слушания, acessed: October 9, 2025), was identified in a map of the Inaglinsky coal mine and processing complex, available on Kolmar's website (see the linked map titled "Карта объектов" or "Map of objects" in English, which is a general map of Kolmar's mining activities in and around the Chulmakan coal deposit: https://web.archive.org/web/20250923210932/https://www.kolmar.ru/activity/maps/. "Карта объектов," Kolmar, accessed: October 9, 2025). According to Kolmar's website description of the Inaglinsky-1 plant (available by clicking and expanding "ОФ «Инаглинская-1»" on the above map, or here directly: https://web.archive.org/web/20250923210950/https://www.kolmar.ru/activity/maps/of-inaglinskaya-1/ "ОФ «Инаглинская-1»," Kolmar, accessed: Oct. 9, 2025), the processing plant handles raw materials from the complex's open-pit mining operations. For this reason, the Inaglinsky-1 plant was presumed to be more closely associated with the Inaglinsky Surface Coal Mine (GEM ID: M0798), rather than the underground mining operations of the same coal complex (such as Inaglinsky Coal Mine 1, GEM ID: M1265).

properties.Emissions Calculation Detail: The latest year for which both emissions data and GCMT production data were available was 2023. The emissions data for this year was 0.00245055 Mt CH4, taken from 'EPA GHG Envirofacts - SUBPART FF - UNDERGROUND COAL MINES table'. The production data for this year was 0.29 Mt coal, taken from data in 'Historic Production (2018-2025)'. Using this data, the emissions factor is 0.008450172413793105 million tonnes of methane per million tonnes of coal.
properties.Measurements Methodology: The emissions data come from quarterly reports to the US Greenhouse Gas Reporting Data Program subpart FF, 'Total Quarterly Net Methane Emissions to the Atmosphere - Calculated Facility Total Quarterly Net CH4'. These data are based on measurements at drainage stations and ventilation shafts and have been annualized by GEM.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
The 'Leer Mine Area' is shown in Figure 1.1-1 General Location Map on page 2 and the 'LEER MINE AREA' is show in Figure 7.5-1 Drillhole Collar Locations, on page 35 of Technical Report Summary, Exhibit 96.1, from February 11, 2022, https://web.archive.org/web/20250507102925/https://minedocs.com/25/Leer-Mine-TR-02112022.pdf. The boundary was extracted from Figure 7.5-1 and has an area of 12,967 acres (52.5 sq km). This area very closely matches the area given in 1.1 PROPERTY DESCRIPTION on page 2, "The Leer Mine permit area includes approximately 12,635 acres of controlled mineral property". The mine mines the Middle Kittanning coal seam.


Important note: the following mine boundaries overlap the mine boundary and care should be taken when attempting methane source attribution: MINE NO. 1 (Upper Freeport coal seam)

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
Section 2.1 Background and Current Operations of the JELLINBAH MINE Water Management Plan BBNE00299_0027-REP-002-0 published 14 November 2024, https://web.archive.org/web/20250905185336/https://jellinbah.com.au/wp-content/uploads/Jellinbah-Mine-WMP-2024.pdf, describes the mine as follows:
"The Jellinbah Coal Mine consist of five (5) distinct operating areas, referred to as South, Central, Central North, Plains, and Mackenzie North (listed north to south). Current operations involve open cut coal mining in the Central, Central North and Mackenzie North areas. The South pit was mined up until 2003 and since used for storage of excess mine affected water.". Figure 2.1 on page 9 of the same document shows the mining leases that comprise Jellinbah mine. The mine boundary includes all mining leases shown in Figure 2.1. The area of the boundary is 84 sq km. 

Mining lease geometries were extracted from the Queensland Mining Leases dataset (https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.data.qld.gov.au/dataset/queensland-mining-and-exploration-tenure-series/resource/f87794b8-7b9a-4732-89bb-56ccb2228d27).

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
The boundary is the complex underground mining area polygon extracted from the West Virginia Geological and Economic Survey (WVGES) resource at https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://atlas.wvgs.wvnet.edu/arcgis/rest/services/Coal_Web_Mercator/All_Mining_WM/MapServer. This resource was filtered for mine_name containing MOUNTAINEER II ALMA MINE. The polygon was deholed and simplified using distance-based simplification with a tolerance of 25m.  The area of the final boundary is 19 sq km. The mine mines the Powellton seam.

properties.Emissions Calculation Detail: The latest year for which both emissions data and GCMT production data were available was 2023. The emissions data for this year was 0.02910653 Mt CH4, taken from 'EPA GHG Envirofacts - SUBPART FF - UNDERGROUND COAL MINES table'. The production data for this year was 3.57 Mt coal, taken from data in 'Historic Production (2018-2025)'. Using this data, the emissions factor is 0.008153089635854342 million tonnes of methane per million tonnes of coal.
properties.Measurements Methodology: The emissions data come from quarterly reports to the US Greenhouse Gas Reporting Data Program subpart FF, 'Total Quarterly Net Methane Emissions to the Atmosphere - Calculated Facility Total Quarterly Net CH4'. These data are based on measurements at drainage stations and ventilation shafts and have been annualized by GEM.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes: This mine operates under the Krasnobrodskoye subsoil land-use license КЕМ11669ТЭ, as identified through the Annual Report of JSC “UK Kuzbassrazrezugol”(Годовой отчет АО «УК Кузбассразрезуголь»), page 3, https://www.archive.org/details/Kuzbassrazrezugol2023, 2023. The license was issued on September 3, 2003, and is valid until December 31, 2032. The boundary was extracted from the NedraExpert portal at https://web.archive.org/web/20251219223515/https://www.nedraexpert.ru/license/144385?ysclid=mjdg4ia9a7745751665. The area between the Krasnobrodskoye and Vakhrushevskoye license boundaries is occupied by subsoil plots (including Karagailinskoye and Novosergeevskoye) classified as part of the Undistributed Subsoil Fund, indicating no active mining operations within this intervening area at the time of review. This was verified through the NedraExpert portal, https://web.archive.org/web/20251217220747/https://www.nedraexpert.ru/subsurface/2100027339/1, https://web.archive.org/web/20251219223601/https://www.nedraexpert.ru/subsurface/2100028211/1. The approximate area of the resulting boundary is 11 square km.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
Section 1.2 Property Description of the Shoal Creek Mine Technical Report Summary S-K 1300 from Feb 18 2022 https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1064728/000106472822000008/btu_20211231xex962.htm : "Shoal Creek controls the majority of the coal within the boundary through coal leases from a variety of private leaseholders and government entities."; and Section 3.2 Property Rights: "The Shoal Creek mineral property boundary encompasses a total of 32,666 acres. Shoal Creek has a total of 14 private mineral leases, 1 federal mineral lease, 2 state mineral leases, and 2 surface rights agreements.  The majority of this mineral control acreage is primarily through lease agreements from RGGS Land and Minerals Ltd, L.P. The sum of the RGGS leases contains 28,517 total mineral acres. The remainder of the mineral lease control is with the United States of America (1,618 acres leased from the Bureau of Land Management), the Alabama State Department of Conservation and Natural Resources (362 acres under the Black Warrior River), and private property leases (1,250 acres from individuals, families, and/or trusts). The remaining 919 acres designated as Not Under Control (NUC) are all located outside of the projected reserve area. The estimated resource areas have three perimeter tracts that are NUC, however based on the previous history with owners, leases to these NUC acres should be obtainable.". Table 3-3. Mineral & Surface Leases and Figure 3-2. Mineral Property Map shows details of these leases. Figure 3-2. Mineral Property Map and Figure 3-3. Surface Property Map both show the Lease Boundary, which is referred to as the 'Property boundary' in Figure 7-1. Exploration Drill Hole Location Map from which this boundary was extracted.
The area of the extracted boundary is 32,143 acres (130 sq km) which is very close to the reported 32,666 acres.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
This mine operates under four adjacent subsoil land-use licenses(GOK Inaglinskiy), ЯКУ 04565 ТЭ, ЯКУ 04564 ТЭ, ЯКУ 04639 ТЭ and ЯКУ 05093 ТЭ, as identified through the Preliminary Environmental Assessment of the Proposed Adjustment to the Inaglinskaya Coal Mine Construction Project
(Предварительная экологическая оценка намечаемой корректировки проекта строительства угольной шахты «Инаглинская»), https://www.archive.org/details/inaglinskaya-coal-mine, page 5, 2021. The license ЯКУ 04565 ТЭ was issued on November 30, 2015, and is valid until December 25, 2026. The license ЯКУ 04564 ТЭ was issued on November 30, 2015, and is valid until June 1, 2025.The license ЯКУ 04639 ТЭ was issued on April 22, 2016, and is valid until April 30, 2041. The license ЯКУ 05093 ТЭ was issued on September 28, 2016, and is valid until February 24, 2032. License issuance and expiration dates were identified through the Rosnedra license registry, “Register of Subsoil Use Licenses as of January 1, 2024” («Реестр лицензий по состоянию на 01.01.2024 г.»), https://www.archive.org/details/register-of-subsoil-use-licenses-as-of-january-1-2024.The boundary for license ЯКУ 04565 ТЭ was extracted from the NedraExpert portal at https://web.archive.org/web/20251223182237/https://www.nedraexpert.ru/license/135788?ysclid=mjiwunfser782625186. The boundary for license ЯКУ 05093 ТЭ was extracted from the NedraExpert portal at <url>.  Polygon boundaries for subsoil licenses ЯКУ 04564 ТЭ and ЯКУ 04639 ТЭ were georeferenced using the Preliminary Environmental Assessment of the Proposed Adjustment to the Inaglinskaya Coal Mine Construction Project («Предварительная экологическая оценка намечаемой корректировки проекта строительства угольной шахты «Инаглинская»), page 94, https://www.archive.org/details/inaglinskaya-coal-mine, 2021. The resulting mine boundary represents the outer perimeter of these four adjacent license areas. The approximate area of the resulting boundary is 170 square km.

The general location of the mine was confirmed in the report and an ANM presentation on the mining project (pg. 1 of "Proyecto La Ramada," 9/19/2022: https://web.archive.org/save/https://mineriaencolombia.anm.gov.co/sites/default/files/docupromocion/Proyecto%20La%20Ramada%2009%2022.pdf ), and the boundary of the mining title was identified using CoMiMo ( https://web.archive.org/web/20250725184307/https://comimo.sig-gis.com/). The mining boundary was then extracted in Google Earth Pro from a Global Forest Watch data set of mining titles in Colombia (see: "Colombia Mining Titles," https://web.archive.org/save/https://data.globalforestwatch.org/datasets/colombia-mining-titles/explore?location=11.275605%2C-86.829278%2C9.97). The approximate area of the boundary polygon is 1.65 square km.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
Figure 2.1 Places affected by the project, page 3, of EIS Assessment Report for the Lake Vermont Meadowbrook Project from 4/2024, 
https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.qld.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0035/477485/lake-vermont-meadowbrook-eis-assessment-report.pdf, describes the existing Lake Vermont mining leases ML 70331, ML 70477 and ML 70528, the outer perimeter of which comprise the extracted mine boundary. This document also describes the mining lease application for the mine extension, known as Meadowbrook Project. It does not appear that this request for expansion has yet been approved. The mining license for the Meadowbrook expansion is ML 700080 and is not included in this boundary. Ongoing information about this expansion can be found at https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.qld.gov.au/environment/management/environmental/eis-process/projects/completed/lake-vermont-meadowbrook-project. The boundary is the outer perimeter of the mining leases ML 70331, ML 70477 and ML 70582. The area of the boundary is approximately 91 sq km. Mining lease geometries were extracted from the Queensland Mining Leases dataset (https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.data.qld.gov.au/dataset/queensland-mining-and-exploration-tenure-series/resource/f87794b8-7b9a-4732-89bb-56ccb2228d27).

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
The Kostenko mine is part of the Karaganda Coal Mines Complex that includes eight underground coal mines and the Vostochnaya coal preparation plant. These mines are: Kostenko, Kuzembaeva, Saranskaya, Abayskaya, Kazakhstanskaya, Lenina, Shakhtinskaya and Tentekskaya coal mines. (https://web.archive.org/web/20250207022321/https://miningdataonline.com/property/1772/Karaganda-Coal-Mines-Complex.aspx). 

The boundary was extracted from the Unified Platform for Subsoil Use, Ministry of Industry and Construction of the Republic of Kazakhstan https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://minerals.e-qazyna.kz/en/contracts-map. Along the northwestern edge of the boundary, there are overlaps with contract objects numbers 472, 421 and 669. The boundary is based on object 144, issued May 12 1997, of work type 'contracts mountain'.

In pgs 4-5 of Appendix 2 of the hearings of the Environmental Impact Assessment on the mining plan of Kostenko mine from 3/2021, https://web.archive.org/web/20250702191012/https://www.gov.kz/uploads/2021/3/6/8b8e5ffe5cc50551785d3490c6c1b385_original.369812.pdf, the dimensions of the combined mine field are given as 4200-7700m x 2500-5000m (10.5 sq km - 38.5 sq km). The area of the extracted boundary is 26.2 sq km which lies within this range.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
The Abayskaya mine is part of the Karaganda Coal Mines Complex that includes eight underground coal mines and the Vostochnaya coal preparation plant. These mines are: Kostenko, Kuzembaeva, Saranskaya, Abayskaya, Kazakhstanskaya, Lenina, Shakhtinskaya and Tentekskaya coal mines, https://web.archive.org/web/20250207022321/https://miningdataonline.com/property/1772/Karaganda-Coal-Mines-Complex.aspx. 

Pages 4-5 of Appendix 1 of the public hearings in the form of open meetings on the draft Environmental Impact Assessment for the Mining Plan for the development of coal reserves at the Abayskaya mine for the period up to 2042, from 4/2021, https://web.archive.org/web/20250703133751/https://www.gov.kz/uploads/2021/4/10/b17a033400f3f948ad85772ba135a382_original.5624626.pdf,  describes the mining boundaries in terms of coal seams, together with coal field dimensions : area no. 1  4800-6000m x 1050-3000m (5-18 sq km), area no. 2  3600-4000m x 1500-2000m (5-8 sq km) - giving a total coal field dimensions range of approx 10 - 26 sq km.

Two adjacent mining contract boundaries for Abayskaya mine can be found using the Unified Platform for Subsoil Use, Ministry of Industry and Construction of the Republic of Kazakhstan https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://minerals.e-qazyna.kz/en/contracts-map , both of which are described as object 144, issued May 12 1997, of work type 'contracts mountain'. The northern contracts boundary is used here because it has an approximate area of 21 sq km which is within the coal field's approximate dimensions of 10 - 26 sq km given in the Appendix 1 reference above.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
The Kazakhstanskaya mine is part of the Karaganda Coal Mines Complex that includes eight underground coal mines and the Vostochnaya coal preparation plant. These mines are: Kostenko, Kuzembaeva, Saranskaya, Abayskaya, Kazakhstanskaya, Lenina, Shakhtinskaya and Tentekskaya coal mines. (https://web.archive.org/web/20250207022321/https://miningdataonline.com/property/1772/Karaganda-Coal-Mines-Complex.aspx). 

The boundary was extracted from the Unified Platform for Subsoil Use, Ministry of Industry and Construction of the Republic of Kazakhstan https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://minerals.e-qazyna.kz/en/contracts-map. The Kazakhstanskaya boundary overlaps with the adjacent Lenina and Tentekskaya mine boundaries. Searching for the Kazakhstanskaya mine contact boundary in the search system was not effective.  Instead, the boundaries for Lenina and Tentekskaya mines were first identified, and then the Kazakhstanskaya deduced. The boundary is based on object 144, issued May 12 1997, of work type 'contracts mountain'.

Section 1 General Information about the Enterprise, on page 14 of the 2020 Environmental Impact Assessment https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.gov.kz/uploads/2021/1/15/a529244bb914a677678f4ebd32056665_original.58771642.pdf refers to the approved technical boundaries in terms of coal seams; the dimensions of the mine field are given as 2500-7000m x 2500-5600m (or 6.25 sq km - 39 sq km). The area of the extracted boundary is 29.5 sq km which lies within this range.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes: Section 2.2 Impact Calculations on page 11 of Disturbance Limits Approach: Maules Creek Coal Mine from September 10 2021, https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://whitehavencoal.com.au/Documentations/Maules%20Creek%20Mine/Approvals/Environmental%20Protection%20and%20Biodiversity%20Conservation%20(EPBC)/MCC-EPBC-Condition%206%20Analysis.pdf?v=1695726601, describes the mine's footprint and how it is expected to change as it is cleared in preparation for mining for year 5 (2018), year 10 (2023) and years 15-21 (2028-2034). This footprint is shown in Figure 2.1 on page 13 shows the footprint. This footprint matches the Maules Creek Project Surface Development Extent shown in Figure 2 on page 11 of MAULES CREEK COAL MINE 2019 ANNUAL REVIEW from 3/2020, https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://whitehavencoal.com.au/Documentations/Maules%20Creek%20Mine/Environmental%20Management,%20Monitoring%20&%20Compliance/Annual%20Reviews/MCC-Annual%20Review%202019.pdf. The mine boundary is the mine's surface development extent as it extends out to 2034. Visual inspection of satellite imagery from 11/2023 shows possible development of the surface in the 2028-2034 region. The area of the boundary is 21 sq km.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes: Section 2.2 Impact Calculations on page 11 of Disturbance Limits Approach: Maules Creek Coal Mine from September 10 2021, https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://whitehavencoal.com.au/Documentations/Maules%20Creek%20Mine/Approvals/Environmental%20Protection%20and%20Biodiversity%20Conservation%20(EPBC)/MCC-EPBC-Condition%206%20Analysis.pdf?v=1695726601, describes the mine's footprint and how it is expected to change as it is cleared in preparation for mining for year 5 (2018), year 10 (2023) and years 15-21 (2028-2034). This footprint is shown in Figure 2.1 on page 13 shows the footprint. This footprint matches the Maules Creek Project Surface Development Extent shown in Figure 2 on page 11 of MAULES CREEK COAL MINE 2019 ANNUAL REVIEW from 3/2020, https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://whitehavencoal.com.au/Documentations/Maules%20Creek%20Mine/Environmental%20Management,%20Monitoring%20&%20Compliance/Annual%20Reviews/MCC-Annual%20Review%202019.pdf. The mine boundary is the mine's surface development extent as it extends out to 2034. Visual inspection of satellite imagery from 11/2023 shows possible development of the surface in the 2028-2034 region. The area of the boundary is 21 sq km.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
According to the Mt Owen/Glendell Open Cut website, https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.glencore.com.au/operations-and-projects/coal/current-operations/mt-owen-glendell-open-cut, the Mount Owen mine is part of the Mount Owen complex which includes Mount Owen, Glendell, and East Ravensworth mines. 

Figure 4 MGO Noise Monitoring locations, page 30, of the Annual Review 2022 Mt Owen / Glendell, https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.glencore.com.au/.rest/api/v1/documents/5be26337fd702c2d67d30e885d615b9f/2022+Annual+review+-+Main+report.pdf, May 31 2023, shows the Mt Owen and Glendell project boundaries. 

These boudaries match extremely closely the Mt Owen DA SSD-5850 and Glendell DA 80/592 boundaries shown in Figure 4: MOC Noise Monitoring Locations, page 39, of the 2018 Mt Owen Complex annual review, https://web.archive.org/web/20250715191617/https://www.glencore.com.au/.rest/api/v1/documents/8678eb560718fa6e5c05b6694cdb5cf4/ANNUAL-REVIEW-2018-Main-Report-amended-June-2019.pdf, March 31 2019.

Note 1: the Ravensworth East mine is part of the Mount Owen complex and within the SSD-5850 boundary as described in the Mount Owen/Glendell 2023 annual report https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.glencore.com.au/.rest/api/v1/documents/34f6615ede78150d537b50a23c2b0259/2023+Annual+Review-+Main+report.pdf, March 28 2024, executive summary on page 5, describing Ravensworth East as part of SSD-5850, the boundary of which is shown in Figure 2: Mt Owen/Glendell Operations Overview and Disturbance as of 31 December on page 16. 

Note 2: the Glendell mine overlaps the Mt Owen boundary but Glendell mine is not included in this boundary because it is a different GEM mine entity.  

Note 3: the mining boundary of Integra Underground Mine, Australia, M4354 overlaps the southeastern section of this boundary. The area of the boundary is approximately 52 sq km.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes: This mine operates under the subsoil land-use licenses MV-000227, MV-005458, MV-006852, MV-012225, and MV-012226, as identified through The Project for Formulation of National Comprehensive Development Plan – Final Report: Sector Report on Crop Farming, Livestock Farming, Mining, Manufacturing and Tourism, prepared by the Ministry of Construction and Urban Development (MCUD), National Development Agency (NDA), and the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA),https://www.archive.org/details/the-project-for-formulation-of-national-comprehensive-development-plan, December 2021. The license MV-000227 was issued on October 8, 1995, and is valid until October 8, 2045. The license MV-005458 was issued on February 25, 2003, and is valid until February 25, 2033. The license MV-006852 was issued on January 28, 2004, and is valid until January 28, 2034. The license MV-012225 was issued on November 22, 2006, and is valid until November 22, 2036. The license MV-012226 was issued on November 22, 2006, and is valid until November 22, 2036.The boundary for the license MV-000227 was extracted from the Opendata Lab Mongolia portal at https://web.archive.org/web/20251219211022/https://opendatalab.mn/mininglicense/227. The boundary for the license MV-005458, was extracted from the Opendata Lab Mongolia portal at https://web.archive.org/web/20251219211422/https://opendatalab.mn/mininglicense/5458. The boundary for the license MV-006852, was extracted from the Opendata Lab Mongolia portal at https://web.archive.org/web/20251219211404/https://opendatalab.mn/mininglicense/6852. The boundary for the license MV-012225, was extracted from the Opendata Lab Mongolia portal at https://web.archive.org/web/20251219211427/https://opendatalab.mn/mininglicense/12225. The boundary for the license MV-012226, was extracted from the Opendata Lab Mongolia portal at https://web.archive.org/web/20251219211439/https://opendatalab.mn/mininglicense/12226. Open pits associated with the Ovoot Tolgoi coal mine may overlap the southern edge of the Nariin Sukhait Coal Mine boundary. The reported mine area is 1,161.4 hectares (11.61 square km); the approximate area of the extracted boundary is 12 square km.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
The boundary is the underground mining area polygon extracted from West Virginia Geological and Economic Survey, Coal Bed Mapping Program GIS data: https://web.archive.org/web/20250220170452/https://atlas.wvgs.wvnet.edu/arcgis/rest/services/Coal_Web_Mercator/All_Mining_WM/MapServer, filtered for mine_name = AFFINITY. The resulting polygon was simplified using distance-based simplification with a tolerance of 25m, and holes deleted. The boundary area is 19.3 sq km. According to information in the same WVGES resource. The mine mines the Pocahontas_3 coal seam. 

Important note: the following mine boundaries overlap the mine boundary and care should be taken when attempting methane source attribution:  Big Stick (Beckley coal seam), Lillybrook Coal, (Pocahontas_6 coal seam), Pemberton mine no. 1 (Beckley coal seam), Tams no 2 (Pocahontas_6 coal seam) and Glen White no 1 & 2 (Beckley coal seam).

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
The boundary is the complex underground mining area polygon extracted from the West Virginia Geological and Economic Survey (WVGES) resource at https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://atlas.wvgs.wvnet.edu/arcgis/rest/services/Coal_Web_Mercator/All_Mining_WM/MapServer. This resource was filtered for mine_name = BLUE CREEK NO. 1, and the resulting polygon was simplified using distance-based simplification with a tolerance of 25m. The mine mines the Stockton coal seam. The area of this boundary is 10 sq km.

Important note: the following mine boundaries overlap the mine boundary and care should be taken when attempting methane source attribution: UNKNOWN (Number_5_Block seam), UNKNOWN (Number_5_Block seam), UNION CARBIDE NO 7A (Number_5_Block seam), AMHURST COAL CO. properties.methane_for_colour_is: GEM Coal Mine Methane Emissions Estimate (M tonnes/yr)

properties.Emissions Calculation Detail: The latest year for which both emissions data and GCMT production data were available was 2023. The emissions data for this year was 0.000154 Mt CH4, taken from 'EPA GHG Envirofacts - SUBPART FF - UNDERGROUND COAL MINES table'. The production data for this year was 0.136 Mt coal, taken from data in 'Historic Production (2018-2025)'. Using this data, the emissions factor is 0.0011323529411764706 million tonnes of methane per million tonnes of coal.
properties.Measurements Methodology: The emissions data come from quarterly reports to the US Greenhouse Gas Reporting Data Program subpart FF, 'Total Quarterly Net Methane Emissions to the Atmosphere - Calculated Facility Total Quarterly Net CH4'. These data are based on measurements at drainage stations and ventilation shafts and have been annualized by GEM.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes: This boundary was extracted from the West Virginia Geological and Economic Survey (WVGES) resource at https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://atlas.wvgs.wvnet.edu/arcgis/rest/services/Coal_Web_Mercator/All_Mining_WM/MapServer. This resource was filtered for mine_name = EAGLE SEAM DEEP MINE, and the resulting polygon was simplified using distance-based simplification with a tolerance of 25m.  The area of this boundary is 1.7 sq km. Satellite imagery for the area including this boundary was scanned for PPSEs - no additional ones were found.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
The boundary is the underground mining area polygon extracted from the West Virginia Geological and Economic Survey (WVGES) resource at https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://atlas.wvgs.wvnet.edu/arcgis/rest/services/Coal_Web_Mercator/All_Mining_WM/MapServer. This resource was filtered for mine_name = JERRY FORK MINE. This name is synonymous with Jerry Fork Eagle mine, with Eagle referring to the coal seam being mined. The resulting polygon was simplified using distance-based simplification with a tolerance of 25m. The area of this boundary is approximately 14 sq km. 

Two other mining boundaries found in WVGES overlap with this boundary: Sugarcamp No. 1 mine, having a small overlap on the southern edge of the boundary; Coalburg No A5, with a relatively small 0.1 sq km boundary that is completely enveloped by the Jerry Fork boundary. Numerous other mines are also closely adjacent to this mine boundary making infrastructure assignment challenging.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:

The area of this boundary is 1 sq km. The mine mines the Number 2 Gas seam.

Important note: the following mine boundaries overlap the mine boundary and care should be taken when attempting methane source attribution: SUPERIOR POCA NO 2 (Number 6 Block seam), BELVA NO 5F (Coalburg seam), NO. 8-C MINE (Eagle seam)

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
Figure 1 Location of the Paso Diablo and Socuy mines, on page 4 of Study of Maracaibo Lake water-coal interaction, accepted 25 May 2006, https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.researchgate.net/publication/289181288_Study_of_Maracaibo_Lake_water-coal_interaction , includes a low resolution potential boundary of the mine. An antialiased version of the figure was used for boundary extraction.

Figure 3 pg 513 of Organic petrology of Paleocene Marcelina Formation coals, Paso Diablo mine, western Venezuela: Tectonic controls on coal type, August 2007, https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0166516206001078, the mine contains two pits, Baqueta Pit to the north, and Paso Diablo Pit to the south. Inspection of Google Earth Pro satellite imagery from 3/9/2025 confirms that the extracted boundary includes both pits.

Due to the age of the resource used for boundary extraction, and the low resolution of the figure used, the coordinates precision has been set to 'estimated'.

The area of the boundary is approximately 81 sq km (8148 hectares).

Mine boundary information was challenging to find due to limited available information.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: Full m: Peak Downs Coal Mine, Australia, M0087
properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes: The Peak Downs mine is sandwiched directly between Caval Ridge mine to the north and Saraji mine to the south. The boundary is derived from existing and authorized surface rights shown in figure 2a of Peak Downs Mine Continuation Project Initial Advice Statement Final Mar 23 2022, https://web.archive.org/web/20250528211924/https://www.bhp.com/-/media/bhp/regulatory-information-media/coal/bma/peak-downs/peak-downs-mine-continuation-project/peak-downs-mine-continuation-project---initial-advice-statement.pdf. Section 3.1 of this document also notes, 'All mining leases include authorisation for ERA 13 (mining black coal). However, this authorisation does not extend to areas within ML 1885 and parts of ML 70411 and ML 1775 where those mining leases do not presently include surface rights and are marked as ‘Nil Surface Rights’ on Figure 2b.  Figure 2a shows the areas of existing surface rights under the mining leases and for which the EA EPML00318213 includes authorisation for ERA 13 (mining black coal)'. properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes: The Peak Downs mine is sandwiched directly between Caval Ridge mine to the north and Saraji mine to the south. The boundary is derived from existing and authorized surface rights shown in figure 2a of Peak Downs Mine Continuation Project Initial Advice Statement Final Mar 23 2022, https://web.archive.org/web/20250528211924/https://www.bhp.com/-/media/bhp/regulatory-information-media/coal/bma/peak-downs/peak-downs-mine-continuation-project/peak-downs-mine-continuation-project---initial-advice-statement.pdf. Section 3.1 of this document also notes, 'All mining leases include authorisation for ERA 13 (mining black coal). However, this authorisation does not extend to areas within ML 1885 and parts of ML 70411 and ML 1775 where those mining leases do not presently include surface rights and are marked as ‘Nil Surface Rights’ on Figure 2b.  Figure 2a shows the areas of existing surface rights under the mining leases and for which the EA EPML00318213 includes authorisation for ERA 13 (mining black coal)'. Prior to adjustments where necessary to support the above information, mining lease geometries were extracted from the Queensland Mining Leases dataset https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.data.qld.gov.au/dataset/queensland-mining-and-exploration-tenure-series/resource/f87794b8-7b9a-4732-89bb-56ccb2228d27. The boundary is comprised of the following mining leases components, with permit names taken from the Queensland Mining Leases dataset: ML 1775, excluding Caval Ridge mine, north of Harrow Creek, and excluding Saraji mine to the south; ML 70403 - excluding Caval Ridge mine, north of Harrow Creek; ML 1783 - Peak Downs industrial mine area; ML 70142 - Boomerang Creek, and excluding Saraji mine to the south; ML 70372 - Peak Downs haul road; ML 70377 - Peak Downs transport overpass; ML 70411 - Peak Downs East, excluding nil surface rights; ML 70412 - Harrow Creek Dam and Red Hill Mine; ML 70463 - Peak Downs West. The area of the boundary is 148 sq km.

One open permit U00500319 for this mine was found on page 92 of FY2024 ANNUAL REPORT AND DIRECTORY OF MINES, https://web.archive.org/web/20250327210504/https://minesafety.wv.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/FY2024-Annual-Report.pdf.pdf. The permit is owned by ARACOMA COAL COMPANY, LLC issued November 2019 and expires November 2029. Other open permits for this mine were searched for but no others were found. The permit boundary polygon was extracted from permit boundaries found in the permit boundary shapefile in https://web.archive.org/web/20250319210132/https://tagis.dep.wv.gov/home/gis%20data. The area of this boundary is 0.19 square kilometers (or 47 acres). The mine mines the Powellton Chilton coal seam. 

Important note: the following mine boundaries overlap the mine boundary and care should be taken when attempting methane source attribution: Lynn Branch No. 2 mine (Eagle seam).

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
The boundary is the complex underground mining area polygon extracted from the West Virginia Geological and Economic Survey (WVGES) resource at https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://atlas.wvgs.wvnet.edu/arcgis/rest/services/Coal_Web_Mercator/All_Mining_WM/MapServer. This resource was filtered for mine_name = MAPLE EAGLE NO. 1, and simplified using distance-based simplification with a tolerance of 100m.  The area of this boundary is 12 sq km. Satellite imagery for the area including this boundary was scanned for PPSEs - no additional ones were found. The mine mines the Eagle seam.

Important note: the following mine boundaries overlap the mine boundary and care should be taken when attempting methane source attribution: POWELLTON NO. 3 (Powellton seam), NO. 24 (Powellton seam), PEABODY COAL (Powellton seam), UNKNOWN (Powellton seam), UNKNOWN (Powellton seam), RIVERTON NO 18 (Peerless seam), RIVERTON NO 35 (Peerless seam), HICKORY CAMP NO 2 (Peerless seam), CHILTON 1A MINE (Lower_Winifrede seam)

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes: The boundary was extracted from a Global Forest Watch (GFW) data set of mining titles in Colombia, which includes shapefiles and proprietary information for the mining title areas in "Columbia Mining Titles," last accessed: Oct. 2, 2025 https://web.archive.org/save/https://data.globalforestwatch.org/datasets/colombia-mining-titles/explore?location=11.275605%2C-86.829278%2C9.97. The GFW data set was opened in Google Earth Pro and the boundary polygons were first identified by location and ownership. Because the GFW data set did not include title numbers, the mining title boundaries were cross-referenced using CoMiMo's interactive map, using the data layer "Títulos mineros" ("mining titles") to confirm the location and boundary shapes of the four relevant mining titles: 092-91 (the original mining lease), FEC-131, 029-91, and 065-92. The mining titles were accessible by selecting the data layer "Títulos mineros" from the layers menu ("Capas") of the CoMiMo map, last accessed: Oct. 2, 2025 https://web.archive.org/save/https://comimo.sig-gis.com/. The original mining title number 092-91 was also confirmed in a 2025 report by Colombia's national mining agency, "Agencia Nacional de Minería", "AUTO PAR BUCARAMANGA No. 0300," June 3, 2025 https://web.archive.org/web/20250725172709/https://www.anm.gov.co/sites/default/files/DocumentosAnm/AUTO-PARB-0300-EXP-092-91-2025.pdf. The boundary is the perimeter of the licensed mining boundaries, including the original contracted mining boundary (No. 092-91) and the expansion mining boundaries (065-92, 029-91 and FEC-131). The area of the mine boundary is approximately 49 square km.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes: The boundary is derived from information found in the Saraji East Mining Lease Project INITIAL ADVICE STATEMENT Final 10 February 2017 report , https://web.archive.org/web/20240403042430/https://www.qld.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0015/108411/saraji_east_ias.pdf. Section 1.2 Project Background, page 2 : "As depicted in Figure 1-1, the Project is located adjacent to the existing Saraji Open-Cut Coal Mine (Saraji Mine). BMA currently operates the Saraji Mine on Mining Lease (ML) 70142, ML 1775, ML 1784, ML 1782, ML 2360, ML 2410, ML 70294, ML 70298 and ML 70328". The Saraji coal mine is sandwiched between Peak Downs coal mine to the north, Norwich Park coal mine to the south, and the Saraji East mine to the east. The location and shape of the southern boundary edge shared with Norwich Park has been estimated, as has the uppermost northeast edge shared with Peak Downs mine. Prior to adjustments where necessary to support the above information, mining lease geometries were extracted from the Queensland Mining Leases dataset, https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.data.qld.gov.au/dataset/queensland-mining-and-exploration-tenure-series/resource/f87794b8-7b9a-4732-89bb-56ccb2228d27. The mining leases components permit names taken from the Queensland Mining Leases dataset are as follows: ML 70142 - boomerang creek;  ML 1775 - Peak Downs;  ML 1784 - Saraji mine;  ML 1782 - Norwich Park;  ML 2360 - Fiddlewood; ML 2410 - Phillips Creek;  ML 70294 - Hakea West;  ML 70298 - Hakea South;  ML 70328 - Tay-Glen. The area of the boundary is 122 sq km.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes: Figure 2.1 Map of the Stockton mine area on page 16 of 'Stockton revisited: The mine and the regulatory minefield', October 2009, https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://ttpp.nz/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Stockton-Mine-PCE-Report.pdf shows the Stockton mine boundary. properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
The boundary is the detailed underground mining area polygon extracted from the West Virginia Geological and Economic Survey (WVGES) resource at https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://atlas.wvgs.wvnet.edu/arcgis/rest/services/Coal_Web_Mercator/All_Mining_WM/MapServer. This resource was filtered for mine_name = HORSE CREEK EAGLE MINE, and the resulting polygon was deholed and simplified using distance-based simplification with a tolerance of 25m.  The area of this boundary is 13.5 sq km. Satellite imagery for the area including this boundary was scanned for additional potential coal mine methane sources - none were found in the boundary. The mine mines the Eagle coal seam.

Important note: the following mine boundaries overlap the mine boundary and care should be taken when attempting methane source attribution: WHITE QUEEN (Peerless seam), ALLEN POWELLTON MINE (Peerless seam), ROWLAND NO 11 (Number_2_Gas seam), OGLEBAY NORTON NO 16 (Winifrede seam), BETHLEHEM MINES NO 117 (Winifrede seam), BETHLEHEM MINES (Winifrede seam), BETHLEHEM MINES NO 3 PORTAL (Winifrede seam), ROWLAND NO 6 (Little_Chilton seam), MARSH FORK (Fire_Clay_Lower_Split_1 seam), SLIP RIDGE CEDAR GROVE MINE (Fire_Clay_Lower_Split_1 seam), ROWLAND NO. 10 (Fire_Clay_Lower_Split_1 seam).

This mine operates under nine adjacent subsoil land-use licenses, MV-011954, MV-011953, MV-016881, MV-016883, MV-011943, MV-011956, MV-016882, MV-000287, MV-011955 as identified through the Erdenes Tavan Tolgoi JSC Annual Report 2019

The internal hole within the polygon corresponds to the Uhaa Khudag area, which is geologically part of the Tavan Tolgoi coal basin but represents a separate mine from the Erdenes Tavan Tolgoi mine complex and is shown at an earlier stage of exploration. The license MV-011954, MV-011953, MV-016881, MV-016883, MV-011956, MV-016882, MV-011955 were issued on August 29, 2006, and is valid until August 29, 2036. properties.Measurements Methodology: The emissions data come from quarterly reports to the US Greenhouse Gas Reporting Data Program subpart FF, 'Total Quarterly Net Methane Emissions to the Atmosphere - Calculated Facility Total Quarterly Net CH4'. Figure 2-2 United Wambo Coal Mine Boundaries, page 3 of the 2021 United Wambo Joint Venture , https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://minedocs.com/23/United-Wambo-Annual-Review-12312021.pdf  shows the SSD 7142 Project Area boundary as of June 29, 2022, including mine lease boundaries in which it sits.

The mine boundary is the SSD 7142 Project Area boundary shown in Figure 2-2 United Wambo Coal Mine Boundaries. The area of the boundary is 31 sq km.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
This boundary was extracted from the West Virginia Geological and Economic Survey (WVGES) resource at https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://atlas.wvgs.wvnet.edu/arcgis/rest/services/Coal_Web_Mercator/All_Mining_WM/MapServer, which was filtered for mine_name ''ALMA NO. 1 MINE''. The resulting polygon adjacent to the mine location was simplified using distance-based simplification with a tolerance of 15m. The area of this boundary is  approximately 3 sq km. The mine mines the Powellton coal seam.

Important note: the following mine boundaries overlap the mine boundary and care should be taken when attempting methane source attribution: Mine No.2 (Douglas coal seam), Culross mine (Lower_Winifrede coal seam), 4 'unknown' mines.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes: One open permit U00300118 for this mine was found on page 91 of https://web.archive.org/web/20250327210504/https://minesafety.wv.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/FY2024-Annual-Report.pdf.pdf. The boundaries are for permit U300118 for Black Eagle mine owned by MARFORK COAL COMPANY, LLC. The permit was issued August 2018 and expires August 2028. Other open permits for this mine were searched for but no others were found. Seven permit boundary polygons were extracted from permit boundaries found in the Mining & Reclamation permit boundary shapefile, described as containing 'extent of the bonded area within which mining activity is permitted to occur.', https://web.archive.org/web/20250319210132/https://tagis.dep.wv.gov/home/gis%20data. The name of the mine in this boundary was 'BLACK EAGLE DEEP MINE' and is assumed to be part of the Black Eagle mine. The area of this boundary is 1.85 square kilometers (or 457 acres).

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 2: notes:
This boundary was extracted from the West Virginia Geological and Economic Survey (WVGES) resource at https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://atlas.wvgs.wvnet.edu/arcgis/rest/services/Coal_Web_Mercator/All_Mining_WM/MapServer . This resource was filtered for mine_name = BLACK EAGLE MINE, and resulting polygon simplified using distance-based simplification with a tolerance of 25m. The mine mines the Eagle coal seam. The area of this boundary is 1.8 sq km.  Satellite imagery for the area including this boundary was scanned for additional PPSEs - none were found in the boundary.

properties.Boundaries and methane sources 1: notes:
